rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjacent tawba verses must share a purpose; otherwise their repetition has no apparent point.
rows.anchor: لكان ذلك تكرارا من غير نكتة ظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s praise of the Prophet’s followers shows he had no sin or deviation, nor nearly inclined away from the right.
rows.anchor: دلالة واضحة على أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لم يكن له في ذلك ذنب ولا زيغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s return in mercy reaches the Prophet, the Emigrants and Helpers, and the three who stayed behind; the first two groups followed him at Tabuk despite some nearly turning back.
rows.anchor: تاب ورجع برحمته رجوعا إلى النبي والمهاجرين والأنصار والثلاثة الذين خلفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three were socially shunned even by their families, grieved continuously, and became certain that repentance was their only refuge; God then guided them to repent and forgave them.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك بسبب أن الناس لم يعاشروهم ولا كلموهم حتى أهلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mercy to the Prophet encompasses mercy to his community; the Prophet is the means through whom blessings reach it.
rows.anchor: فالتوبة عليهم توبة عليه فهو صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم الواسطة في نزول الخيرات والبركات إلى أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two later mentions of God’s tawba detail the earlier summary: God first guides and enables repentance, then accepts the servant’s repentance and forgives.
rows.anchor: توبة العبد محفوفة بتوبتين من الرب تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the first occurrence, no sin requiring forgiveness is attributed to the Emigrants and Helpers; the possible inclination to deviate points instead to God’s prior enabling guidance.
rows.anchor: لم يذكر منهم فيها ذنبا يستغفرون له حتى تكون توبته عليهم توبة قبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God’s tawba precedes their repentance, it means the first tawba, guidance that enables them to repent.
rows.anchor: فتوبته تعالى قبل توبتهم ليست إلا التوبة الأولى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God compassionate and merciful supports the enabling-guidance reading, since the verse names no attribute explicitly denoting acceptance.
rows.anchor: حيث لم يذكر من اسمائه ما يدل بلفظه على قبول توبتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “so that they repent” refers to the three left behind; they repent after God guides them, and God then accepts and forgives.
rows.anchor: ليتوب الثلاثة فيتوب عليهم ويغفر لهم إنه هو التواب الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the wording alone does not state acceptance, the story is established by transmission and the verse’s broad tawba language and final names make rejection of their repentance impossible; 4:17 confirms acceptance.
rows.anchor: فمن المحال أن يردهم الله من بابه خائبين وهو التواب الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that “so that they repent” means God merely made repentance easy is a weak interpretation.
rows.anchor: ثم سهل الله عليهم التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects interpreting their repentance as a return to their pre-sin condition.
rows.anchor: الرجوع إلى حالتهم الأولى قبل المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also rejects taking the pronoun as referring to all believers, who would repent after hearing that God accepts repentance.
rows.anchor: قول آخرين إن الضمير في { ليتوبوا } راجع إلى المؤمنين والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this context, zann conveys certainty by contextual implication, not by the word’s lexical meaning.
rows.anchor: أن الظن يفيد في الآية مفاد العلم لا لدلالة لفظية بل لخصوص المورد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sidq first means a report matching reality, then broadly includes acting according to one’s belief and sincerely carrying out one’s resolve.
rows.anchor: توسع في معنى الصدق فعد الإنسان صادقا إذا طابق خبره الخارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrestricted commands to fear God and be with the truthful require following truthful people in word and deed; “being with” means practical companionship, not becoming like them.
rows.anchor: والمعية هي المصاحبة في العمل وهو الاتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medina’s people and nearby Bedouins may not put their own comfort before the Prophet by abandoning him amid campaign dangers and hardship.
rows.anchor: وليس لهم أن يشتغلوا بأنفسهم عن نفسه فيتركوه عند مخاطر المغازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God records thirst, fatigue, hunger, every place trodden to anger the disbelievers, and every gain from them as righteous work, whose reward is not lost.
rows.anchor: في كل مصيبة تصيبهم في الجهاد من جوع وعطش وتعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every small or large expenditure and every valley crossed is recorded for them so God can reward their best deeds.
rows.anchor: نفقاتهم صغيرة يسيرة كانت أو كبيرة خطيرة وكذا كل واد قطعوه فإنه مكتوب لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the best reward is named because workers most desire it; alternatively, rewarding the best deeds entails rewarding the rest.
rows.anchor: لأن رغبة العامل عاكفة عليه، أو لأن الجزاء بأحسنها يستلزم الجزاء بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation identifies the best deeds with jihad, since it is the hardest work and sustains the religious call.
rows.anchor: المراد بأحسن الأعمال الجهاد في سبيل الله لكونه أشقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also offers two related readings: reward is the deed returning to God, or God removes defects from good works so they become best before rewarding them.
rows.anchor: يغفر الله سبحانه سيئاتهم المشوبة بأعمالهم الحسنة ويستر جهات نقصها

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports that 9:111 was revealed while the Prophet was in the mosque; an Anṣari asked if it had been revealed and called it a profitable sale with no cancellation.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال نزلت هذه الآية على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو في المسجد

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq replies to ʿAbbād al-Baṣrī’s objection that Zayn al-ʿAbidin chose Hajj over difficult jihad: jihad with people bearing the traits in 9:112 is better than Hajj.
rows.anchor: إذا رأينا هؤلاء الذين هذه صفتهم فالجهاد معهم أفضل من الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports define the community’s “journeying” variously as worship in mosques, fasting, or jihad in God’s path; the author notes that this was discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: سياحة أمتي في المساجد

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra attributes to the Prophet the interpretation that those who journey are the fasting.
rows.anchor: أن السائحين هم الصائمون

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: A report from Abu Umama attributes to the Prophet the interpretation that the community’s journeying is jihad in God’s path; al-Majmaʿ also reports the accusative reading from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq.
rows.anchor: أن سياحة أمتي الجهاد في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: أبوه
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab’s father reports that, as Abu Talib was dying, the Prophet urged him to profess God’s oneness, but Abu Jahl and ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Umayya pressed him to remain on ʿAbd al-Muttalib’s religion; he refused.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب عن أبيه قال لما حضرت أبا طالب الوفاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says the Prophet then vowed to seek forgiveness for Abu Talib until forbidden, whereupon 9:113 and 28:56 were revealed; other Sunni routes give a similar account, sometimes adding that Muslims imitated him for their polytheist parents.
rows.anchor: لأستغفرن لك ما لم أنه عنك

rows.speaker: أهل البيت عليهم السلام
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai says reports from the Imams consistently hold that Abu Talib was Muslim but concealed his faith to protect the Prophet; his poetry supports monotheism and belief in prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقد اتفقت الرواية عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أنه كان مسلما

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Baqir explains that al-awwāh means one who supplicates.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر قال الأواه الدعاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan reports that Muslims who died before the obligations were revealed prompted a question about their status, followed by the revelation of 9:115.
rows.anchor: مات قوم من المسلمين على الإسلام قبل أن تنزل الفرائض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas connects the verse to taking ransom from captives at Badr before permission; God does not punish a people before clarifying what they must avoid.
rows.anchor: نزلت حين أخذوا الفداء من المشركين يوم الأسارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two reports are applications of the verse rather than occasions of revelation in the technical sense, and its continuity with the preceding verses is clear.
rows.anchor: الروايتين أنهما من التطبيق دون النزول بمعناه المصطلح عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding phrase about worldly enjoyment explains in detail why people’s transgression harms themselves, making the example a specification of the general statement.
rows.anchor: تفصيل لإجمال قوله { إنما بغيكم على أنفسكم } فقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life is illustrated through a sustained representational analogy of rain and flourishing vegetation, not a simple one-to-one comparison of isolated things.
rows.anchor: وهو من الاستعادة التمثيلية وليس من تشبيه المفرد بالمفرد من شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-zukhruf means ornament and beauty; lam taghn means that a place remained settled there for a long time.
rows.anchor: من غني في المكان إذا أقام فيه فأطال المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duʿa is broader than vocal address: it draws the addressee’s attention to what is called toward, by speech, gesture, or other means; nida is spoken and loud.
rows.anchor: والدعاء يكون باللفظ والإشارة وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s call can be creative, bringing a thing toward what He wills, or legislative, summoning people through revealed commands; human worship is inwardly supplication through servitude.
rows.anchor: والدعاء في الله سبحانه تكويني وهو إيجاد ما يريده لشيء

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: Al-Manar argues that prescribed worship is not all invocation: fasting is neither linguistically nor legally called duʿa; duʿa is innate worship and a central part of obligation.
rows.anchor: فإن الصيام لا يسمى دعاء لغة ولا شرعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai rejects that limitation as arising from equating duʿa with verbal calling for a request and overlooking its broader meaning.
rows.anchor: ومنشأ خطئه زعمه أن معنى الدعاء هو النداء للطلب

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines salam as freedom from outward and inward harms; salam and salama are equivalent, while peace is safety in itself and security is safety relative to a threat.
rows.anchor: أصل في معنى السلام على ما ذكره الراغب في المفردات هو التعري عن الآفات الظاهرة والباطنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is named al-Salam because His essence contains no evil; Paradise is the House of Peace because it has no evil or harm, ultimately for the same reason.
rows.anchor: والسلام من أسمائه تعالى لأن ذاته المتعالية نفس الخير الذي لا شر فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrestricted House of Peace is Paradise, since peace in this world is only relative and mixed with limits and opposing conditions.
rows.anchor: فما من شيء إلا وهو مزاحم ممنوع من بعض ما يحبه ويهواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Paradise the House of Peace at their Lord implies their nearness to God’s presence without heedlessness; guidance and the straight path were discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: في تقييد دار السلام بكونها عند ربهم دلالة على قرب الحضور وعدم غفلتهم عنه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi reports that Quraysh demanded a different Qur’an, and the response recalled the Prophet’s forty years among them before revelation; al-Tabatabai says the report’s fit is unclear.
rows.anchor: فقد لبثت فيكم أربعين سنة قبل أن يوحى إلي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits from al-Sadiq that the Prophet repeatedly feared punishment if he disobeyed God until the Conquest surah came; the author finds the report problematic.
rows.anchor: إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: Urwa reports that ʿIkrima fled at the conquest, then, after sailors insisted only God could be invoked at sea, reasoned that God was alone on land too and accepted Islam; the story has many variants.
rows.anchor: والله لئن كان في البحر وحده إنه لفي البر وحده

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says three wrongs return upon their perpetrator: broken pledges, transgression, and plotting; al-Tabatabai notes a parallel Prophetic report from Anas.
rows.anchor: ثلاث يرجعن على صاحبهن النكث والبغي والمكر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet then cites 10:23, 35:43, and 48:10 to show that transgression, plotting, and broken pledges return upon those who commit them.
rows.anchor: ثم تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم { يا أيها الناس إنما بغيكم على أنفسكم }

rows.speaker: محمد بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Baqir teaches that asking is the best worship and supplication can avert decree; charity brings good reward quickly, while oppression brings swift punishment.
rows.anchor: ما من عبادة أفضل من أن تسأل، وما يدفع القضاء إلا الدعاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the Prophet’s saying that if one mountain wronged another, the wrongdoer would be crushed.
rows.anchor: لو بغى جبل على جبل لدك الباغي منهما

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Baqir explains that al-Salam is God and His abode, created for His friends, is Paradise.
rows.anchor: إن السلام هو الله عز وجل وداره التي خلقها لأوليائه الجنة

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: A report attributed to Zayd ibn Ali interprets the House of Peace as Paradise and the straight path as the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib.
rows.anchor: يعني ولاية علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the latter report is a Companion-level stopping point, the author treats it as application or an inner meaning; other reports convey similar interpretations.
rows.anchor: إن كانت الرواية موقوفة فهي من الجري أو من الباطن من معنى القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People divide into believers in the Qur’an and unbelievers; calling the latter corrupters identifies corruption as the source of their denial.
rows.anchor: فتحصل من ذلك أن الذين يكذبون بما في القرآن إنما كذبوا به لأنهم مفسدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the claim that the verse predicts the Prophet’s people will split into believers and unbelievers unlike earlier fully destroyed peoples; that meaning is outside the wording.
rows.anchor: فهو معنى خارج عن مدلول الآية البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they deny him, the Prophet should state that each side answers for its own deeds; this is disassociation to preserve truth when people refuse its call.
rows.anchor: فالطريق هو حمل الناس عليه إن حملوا وإلا فالتبري منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their listening without understanding is deafness of the heart, as the phrase about not reasoning indicates; the Prophet cannot make them hear in that sense.
rows.anchor: قرينة على أن المراد بنفي السمع نفي ما يقارنه من تعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about people looking at the Prophet parallels the preceding verse about hearing: their inward blindness prevents guidance.
rows.anchor: الكلام فيها نظير الكلام في سابقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not wrong people by taking their sight or hearing; their deprivation follows from their own injustice.
rows.anchor: من آثار ظلمهم أنفسهم من غير أن يكون الله تعالى ظلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses the phrase about their short stay as a circumstantial clause describing them as they are gathered.
rows.anchor: كأن لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls the alternatives that the brief-lifetime phrase modifies the day or deleted verbal noun, and that recognition modifies the hour, remote and unsupported by the wording.
rows.anchor: وهما من الاحتمالات البعيدة التي لا يساعد عليها اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers lose when gathered because they see worldly life as only an hour and recognize one another without forgetting or denying each other.
rows.anchor: يعدونها كمكث ساعة من النهار وهم يتعارفون بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage returns to the surah’s opening theme of meeting God: the future unveiling of religion will expose worldly life’s brevity and the ultimate sovereignty of the One.
rows.anchor: فإنهم سوف يحشرون إلى الله فيشاهدون أن ليست الحياة الدنيا إلا متاعا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised judgment is a special feature of messengership rather than prophethood.
rows.anchor: وهذا القضاء المذكور في الآية من خواص الرسالة دون النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contemporary polytheists ask when the worldly judgment between them and the Prophet will occur, seeking his destruction and the believers’ deliverance; the eschatological reading and earlier nations as questioners do not fit the reply.
rows.anchor: والسائلون هم بعض المشركين من معاصري النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question taunts the Prophet to hurry God’s promised destruction, as does their demand for angels in 15:7.
rows.anchor: فهلا عجل لكم ذلك - وذلك أن كلامهم مسوق سوق الاستعجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet cannot bring himself harm or benefit except by God’s will; all command belongs to God, so demanding that he hasten judgment is ignorant.
rows.anchor: أن يبدأهم في الجواب ببيان أنه لا يملك لنفسه ضرا حتى يدفعه عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The specific time is unseen and known only to God, as the surah has already stated.
rows.anchor: فإنه من الغيب الذي لا يعلمه إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every community has a fixed lifespan: once its term arrives it can neither be delayed nor advanced, and this law also applies to the Prophet’s people.
rows.anchor: لكل أمة أجل إذا جاء أجلهم فلا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Communities have a collective life beyond individual lifetimes, with their own lifespan, fortune, suffering, duties, guidance, error, reward, and punishment under divine governance.
rows.anchor: لكل أمة حياة اجتماعية وراء الحياة الفردية التي لكل واحد من أفرادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruined settlements and Qur’anic histories of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud, Abraham’s people, Lot’s cities, and Pharaoh’s Copts show that earlier peoples perished only after messengers brought proofs and most people rejected them.
rows.anchor: التاريخ ويفصح عنه الآثار من ديارهم الخربة ومساكنهم الخالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this community too divided over the truth, God will judge it as He judged earlier peoples; the warning reaches wrongdoers among the faithful as well as polytheists.
rows.anchor: سيقضي الله بين رسوله وبينهم فيأخذهم بما أخذ به من خلت من قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the belief that this community is immune from worldly punishment because it is mercied for the Prophet’s sake; honor with God comes only through piety.
rows.anchor: لا كرامة عند الله إلا بالتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-an now is lengthened from two hamzas; Pharaoh is rebuked for professing faith only when punishment and death surround him, after a life of disobedience and corruption.
rows.anchor: أتؤمن بالله الآن وهو حين أدركك العذاب ولا إيمان وتوبة حين غشيان العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the moment Moses and Aaron had asked God to bring about: Pharaoh would be barred from believing until punishment came, when faith and repentance could no longer help.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الذي كان موسى وهارون سألاه ربهما أن يأخذه بعذاب أليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being rescued with his body implies Pharaoh had another aspect, the soul or spirit, which was taken at death; the soul is the perceiving and willing self, while the body is its instrument.
rows.anchor: وتنجيته ببدنه تدل على أن له أمرا آخر وراء البدن فقده بدنه بغشيان العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Personal identity belongs to the soul rather than the changing body: otherwise a person could not remain answerable for actions performed in youth after the body’s parts changed.
rows.anchor: فلو كان زيد هو البدن الذي ولدته امه يوم ولدته والاسم له لكان غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus “We will save you in your body” means God brought Pharaoh’s body out of the sea; because soul and body are united, saving the body is a kind of saving him.
rows.anchor: فمعنى { ننجيك ببدنك } نخرج بدنك من اليم وننجيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here rijz means doubt and misgiving, the opposite of faith, as in 6:125.
rows.anchor: وقد أريد في الآية بالرجس ما يقابل الإيمان من الشك والريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who do not reason are rejecters whose hearts God has sealed, as described in 9:93.
rows.anchor: أهل التكذيب بآيات الله من جهة أنهم ممن حقت عليه كلمة العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Looking at the heavens and earth means observing diverse creatures, each a sign calling people to faith; the question about signs and warnings is rhetorical lament because determined unbelievers gain nothing from them.
rows.anchor: من المخلوقات المختلفة المتشتة التي كل واحد منها آية من آيات الله تعالى تدعو إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read the clause about signs and warnings as a negative statement rather than an interrogative.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن ما نافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since signs do not benefit them, the disbelievers await only the punitive days suffered by earlier peoples; the commanded waiting anticipates that punishment and a faith that will come too late.
rows.anchor: أي إذا لم تغن الآيات والنذر عنهم شيئا وهم لا يؤمنون البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Then We save Our messengers and those who believed” completes the threat about earlier peoples; “wait” interrupts it as a reply directed to the deniers.
rows.anchor: الجملة تتمة صدر الآية السابقة وقوله { قل فانتظروا } الخ، جملة معترضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interruption suits the warning because the Prophet awaits the judgment with them, while he and the believers—not the Prophet alone—await deliverance from punishment.
rows.anchor: وأما تنجيته وتنجية المؤمنين به فإن المنتظر لها هو النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والمؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God saved earlier messengers and their believers when punishment came, He promises to save the believers of this community; “as a true obligation upon Us” is an absolute-object construction and “the believers” refers to this community.
rows.anchor: كما كنا ننجي الرسل والذين آمنوا في الأمم السابقة عند نزول العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may subtly suggest that the Prophet will not live to see the judgment, since only this community’s believers are named; the author presents this as a possible inference, supported by repeated statements about dying before the return.
rows.anchor: وليس من البعيد أن يستفاد من قوله { ننج المؤمنين } أن فيه تلويحا

rows.speaker: أخيه
rows.claim: Musa ibn Muhammad asked his brother, al-Rida, about the conditional in 10:94; the response says it addresses the Prophet without implying doubt and answers objectors who wondered why a messenger was a human who ate and walked in markets.
rows.anchor: قال موسى فسألت أخي عن ذلك

rows.speaker: أخيه
rows.claim: The response says the conditional was used to persuade the audience, like inviting mutual imprecation in 3:61; the Prophet knew he was truthful but wanted to be fair-minded.
rows.anchor: ولو قال تعالوا نبتهل فنجعل لعنة الله عليكم لم يكونوا يجيئون للمباهلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Saduq also transmits the question-and-answer report in Maʿani; the author says it accords with his previous interpretation.
rows.anchor: ورواه الصدوق في المعاني بإسناده عن موسى بن محمد بن علي

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Another report says the verse came on the Night Journey, when the Prophet was to ask the souls of earlier prophets; al-Tabatabai finds this poorly matched to the wording.
rows.anchor: لكن في انطباقه على لفظ الآية خفاء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Qatada transmits the Prophet’s statement, “I do not doubt and do not ask.”
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال ذكر لنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الرضا
rows.claim: Al-Rida recounts that Jonah warned his people; as punishment approached, they separated children from parents and animals from offspring, cried to God, and the punishment was withheld.
rows.anchor: ففرقوا بينهم وبين أولادهم وبين البهائم وأولادها

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says caution cannot avert destiny, but supplication can, citing Nineveh’s deliverance after its people believed.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال إن الحذر لا يرد القدر، وإن الدعاء يرد القدر

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai notes that a similar saying is transmitted from the Prophet through Aisha.
rows.anchor: وروى ما في معناه عن ابن النجار عن عائشة عن النبي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says rijz is doubt and that the Imams never doubt their religion.
rows.anchor: الرجس هو الشك ولا نشك في ديننا أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith or surah must have a substantial, coherent purpose; otherwise opponents could answer the Qur’an’s challenge by assembling isolated verses with no unified aim.
rows.anchor: ولولا ذلك لم يتم التحدي بالآيات القرآنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks for eloquent speech about divine aims; the whole Qur’an uniquely covers the guidance, beliefs, virtues, and rules humanity needs until the resurrection.
rows.anchor: كتاب فيه ما يحتاج إليه نوع الإنسان إلى يوم القيامة من معارف أصلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A surah has its own unified divine purpose, while a set of ten or twenty surahs displays varied aims; this variety makes accidental uniqueness still less plausible.
rows.anchor: والعدة من السور كالعشر والعشرين منها تختص بخاصة أخرى وهي بيان فنون من المقاصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even one surah’s eloquent, truthful meanings and noble qualities are not plausibly the product of chance; it is intentionally composed around a purpose.
rows.anchor: وما هذا شأنه لا يقع عن مجرد الاتفاق والصدفة من غير أن يكون مقصودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failure of the Prophet or believers to answer a challenge does not prove divine origin unless the opponents first invited their alleged partners to compete; that did not occur.
rows.anchor: ولم يتحقق من المشركين دعوة على هذه الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed interpretation inserts an unstated condition and asks believers to base certainty on a hypothetical; a genuine challenge says they neither can nor will answer.
rows.anchor: فإن لم يستجيبوا لكم ولن يستجيبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawfiya means delivering someone’s due in full, while bakhs is reduction of recompense.
rows.anchor: التوفية إيصال الحق إلى صاحبه وإعطاؤه له بكماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who choose worldly life receive the worldly results they seek when other causes cooperate; deeds produce the goal for which they were intended, while unintentional good works earn no afterlife reward.
rows.anchor: ما لم يقصد به وجه الله ودار ثوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they did not intend an afterlife goal, these people have only Hell there; their deeds are erased and rendered void, like wood consumed by fire.
rows.anchor: تأكل جميع أعمالهم في الحياة كما تأكل النار الحطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two clauses about deeds being erased and made void explain what it means to have only the Fire in the afterlife; another passage calls Hell the abode of ruin.
rows.anchor: وبذلك يظهر أن كلا من قوله { وحبط ما صنعوا فيها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly results mean the effects of deeds under the causal order, not whatever the actor hopes to obtain; the Qur’an says one receives some of the worldly harvest and receives what God wills.
rows.anchor: توفية نتائجها وإيصال الآثار التي لها بحسب نظام الأسباب والمسببات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verses state a divine truth: God’s giving from worldly aims is partial and governed by His will and the operation of causes.
rows.anchor: أن الآيتين أعني قوله { من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها نوف إليهم أعمالهم }

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Baqir reports from Jabir that polytheists bent their backs and covered themselves to hide from the Prophet near the Kaaba; the verse was revealed about them.
rows.anchor: أخبرني جابر بن عبد الله أن المشركين كانوا إذا مروا برسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو رزين
rows.claim: Abu Razin gives a parallel account: a person would bend his back and cover himself with a garment.
rows.anchor: كان أحدهم يحني ظهره ويستغشي بثوبه

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ reports a variant reading of the verb from Zayn al-Abidin, al-Baqir, and al-Sadiq.
rows.anchor: روي عن علي بن الحسين وأبي جعفر وجعفر بن محمد عليهم السلام يثنوني

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: A needy Bedouin asked the Prophet to pray for his large family; the Prophet said God guarantees every creature’s provision, prayed for him, and he later became wealthy.
rows.anchor: ما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها ويعلم مستقرها ومستودعها

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud transmits a Prophetic report that a person’s need leads him to the land where his lifespan will end; the author says it does not clearly explain the verse.
rows.anchor: والرواية غير ظاهرة في تفسير الآية

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage, the Prophet said no soul dies before receiving its full provision; believers should seek it properly, since God apportioned lawful provision and disobedience cannot improve the timing.
rows.anchor: أنه لا تموت نفس حتى تستكمل رزقها فاتقوا الله وأجملوا في الطلب

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: The same report warns that violating God’s protection to seize unlawful provision cuts lawful provision and brings accountability; al-Tabatabai calls the report famous in many Sunni and Shiʿi routes.
rows.anchor: هتك حجاب ستر الله عز وجل وأخذه من غير حله قص به من رزقه الحلال

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says God apportioned provisions but left a great surplus available to no one, citing the command to ask God for His bounty; the author says it is also transmitted from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: إن الله قسم الأرزاق بين عباده وأفضل فضلا كبيرا لم يقسمه بين أحد
